correctness.rationale: Direct multiplication gives A-Ahat=(ab/d)vv^T with ||v||=1 and d=au_1^2+bu_2^2. Real Gaussian directions induce Beta(1/2,1/2) coordinate energy, yielding the explicit CDF and q-moment integral. Standard angular integrals give E R=sqrt(kappa) and E R^2=(kappa+1)sqrt(kappa)/2. Beta dominated convergence, boundary logarithm and rescaling t=s/kappa give the full moment trichotomy, including constants. Strict convexity plus isotropy E T=1/2 proves the sharp sign-law minimum for all q>0. Rational residual tests and deterministic Gaussian angular quadrature passed; neither is substituted for an infinite proof. At kappa=1 minimizer uniqueness is deliberately excluded.

value.rationale: The no-oversampling one-probe regime is natural for minimum-pass low-rank Nyström and sits outside standard oversampled guarantees. Its exact risk quantifies rare near-orthogonal Gaussian directions: despite bounded risk at every finite condition number, relative mean-squared error grows as kappa^(3/2)/2 and all error-moment orders change at q=1/2. A complete equality characterization identifies angle-balanced sampling as optimally robust among isotropic direction laws on a diagonal two-eigenvalue benchmark, giving a concrete nontrivial distribution-design comparison. This does not purport to optimize unknown-eigenbasis, higher-rank, or floating-point deployments.
